message:
Please review the following document.

Here is how its author describes it:

<author>
This bid is unusual in that it is not based on assumptions about demand: we tested the exact opening pattern at Ashgrove before asking for a penny, and measured the results hour by hour. The pilot showed strong uptake, with evening visits running close to daytime levels and Sunday sessions very popular with families, and new memberships up by about two-thirds on the year before. That gives Members real local evidence that the hours will be used. The costing is equally careful. Staffing is built up from first principles, hours times staff times weeks times branches at the correct graded rate with on-costs, and utilities are taken from actual pilot spend rather than estimates, all of which sums to £174,000. We also looked seriously at the cheaper self-service alternative and explain why it would cost more once building works are included. I am confident this is a well-tested, carefully costed proposal that delivers on the Council Plan.
</author>

<document>
Budget Justification: Extended Opening Hours at Five Branch Libraries, 2027-28
Library Services, Westmoor Borough Council, September 2026

1. Request
Library Services requests a growth bid of £174,000 in the 2027-28 revenue budget to extend opening hours at five branch libraries (Ashgrove, Fenwick, Holt Lane, Kingsmead and Millbrook) by ten hours a week each, from 38 to 48 hours.

2. Rationale
The five branches currently close at 5 pm on weekdays and do not open on Sundays. Residents' surveys have repeatedly identified opening hours as the main barrier to library use among working-age adults: in the 2025 Residents' Survey, 44% of non-users aged 25-54 said the library "is never open when I can go". The Council Plan commits to increasing library use among working-age residents and to supporting adult learning and job-seeking.

Each branch would add late opening until 8 pm on Tuesdays and Thursdays (six additional hours) and Sunday opening from 11 am to 3 pm (four additional hours).

3. Evidence from the Ashgrove pilot
From October 2025 to March 2026, Ashgrove trialled exactly this pattern, funded from one-off underspends.

Table 1. Ashgrove pilot: average visits per opening hour, October 2025 to March 2026
Time slot | Visits per hour
Weekday 9 am - 12 pm | 46
Weekday 12 pm - 5 pm | 58
Tuesday and Thursday 5 pm - 8 pm (new) | 21
Saturday 9 am - 1 pm | 64
Sunday 11 am - 3 pm (new) | 52

Over the pilot, Ashgrove recorded 1,140 new library memberships, compared with 690 in the same months a year earlier. Sunday sessions were particularly popular with families, and a weekly job club in the Thursday evening slot was fully booked from its third week.

Evening visits at Ashgrove averaged close to the weekday daytime level, which shows that there is strong latent demand for evening opening and that the new hours will be well used across all five branches.

4. Costs
Additional hours need two staff on duty at all times, in line with the Council's lone-working policy. Staffing is calculated on 50 weeks a year, allowing for bank holiday closures.

Table 2. Cost of extended hours, five branches
Item | Basis | Cost
Staffing | 10 hours x 2 staff x 50 weeks x 5 branches = 5,000 hours at £24.80 per hour (including on-costs) | £124,000
Utilities and caretaking | £6,500 per branch | £32,500
Self-service kiosk upgrades (maintenance contract) | 5 branches | £7,500
Total | | £174,000

The staffing rate is the mid-point of the Library Assistant grade plus 28% on-costs and an enhancement for Sunday working. Utilities and caretaking costs are based on the actual additional costs recorded at Ashgrove during the pilot, scaled to a full year.

5. Value for money
At current visit rates, the extra hours across the five branches would generate roughly 84,000 additional visits a year, at a cost of around £2 per visit. This compares favourably with the borough's average cost per library visit of £3.40.

6. Alternatives considered
We considered opening the branches with self-service access only in the extra hours, as some authorities have done. This would cut staffing costs by around two-thirds, but the Council's insurers have advised that unstaffed opening would require building alterations and CCTV at an estimated £60,000 per branch, and it would not support the job club and family activities that drove much of the pilot's success.

7. Risks
Recruitment. We expect to fill most additional hours from existing part-time staff who have asked for more hours, as happened during the pilot.
Demand at other branches. Ashgrove is our busiest branch, and demand at the other four may be lower. We will review usage after six months.

8. Conclusion
The twelve-month Ashgrove pilot has demonstrated strong demand for evening and Sunday opening, with new memberships up by two-thirds and evening use close to daytime levels. We ask Members to approve a growth bid of £174,000 to extend this successful model to all five branches from April 2027.
</document>
response:
This bid asks for £174,000 a year to open five branch libraries ten more hours a week: Tuesday and Thursday evenings until 8 pm, and Sundays 11 am–3 pm. It relies on a pilot of the same pattern at Ashgrove and a bottom-up costing.

Testing the exact pattern before bidding is good practice, and the Sunday and job-club results are strong. But the bid has four problems:

- The costs in Table 2 add up to £164,000, not £174,000.
- The evening figures in the bid's own table contradict its main evidence claim.
- The pilot was six months, not twelve.
- Ashgrove's demand is applied to four quieter branches.

The data actually support Sunday opening much more strongly than evening opening, and a phased bid would be easier to defend.

## 1. Errors of fact and arithmetic

**The total is £10,000 too high.** £124,000 + £32,500 + £7,500 = **£164,000**. Either the total is wrong or a £10,000 line is missing. The author's description also says the items "sum to £174,000."

**Evening use is not "close to daytime levels."**
- Evenings averaged **21 visits an hour**. Weekday daytime averaged about **54** (46 in the morning, 58 in the afternoon, weighted by hours).
- So evening use is about **40% of daytime**.
- Sunday, at 52 an hour, *is* close to daytime use. The bid has attached Sunday's result to the evenings.
- §3 concludes from this that there is "strong latent demand" for evenings across all five branches. The author's description repeats the same claim.

**The pilot was six months.** It ran October 2025 to March 2026, so the conclusion's "twelve-month Ashgrove pilot" is wrong.

## 2. The visit and value-for-money figures are generous

**The 84,000 is correct for Ashgrove only.** The arithmetic holds: (6 h × 21 + 4 h × 52) × 50 weeks × 5 branches ≈ 83,500. But it assumes all five branches match Ashgrove, which §7 says is the busiest branch. If the other four see 60% of Ashgrove's demand, visits fall to about 70,000. If they see half, visits fall to about 67,000.

**Not every visit is additional.** Some people who now come on Sunday or in the evening would previously have come on a weekday or Saturday. Comparing each time slot at Ashgrove before and during the pilot would show how much use simply moved.

**Marginal cost is compared with average cost.** The £3.40 borough average includes buildings, management and stock. The extra hours carry none of those, so their cost per visit will always look lower. A fairer comparison is between different ways of adding hours.

**The memberships rise isn't tied to the new hours.** New memberships rose from 690 to 1,140 (+65%), but nothing shows those people joined during or because of the new hours. The report should check what else changed at Ashgrove that winter, such as publicity, school visits or the job club itself.

## 3. Costing points

**Annual leave isn't covered.** If part-time staff take on 5,000 extra hours, their paid leave rises in proportion. Those hours still have to be staffed while they're away, so the paid hours, and the cost, will be roughly 10–15% above £124,000 unless cover is already built into the £24.80 rate.

**50 weeks may undercount.** Most bank holidays fall on Mondays or Fridays, not on the new Tuesday, Thursday and Sunday sessions. Unless the branches close for two weeks at Christmas, more like 51–52 weeks will be worked.

**The £24.80 rate needs explaining.** It includes a Sunday enhancement, but Sundays are only 4 of the 10 extra hours. The bid should state whether the rate is a blended average across all hours, and whether evening work also carries an enhancement.

**Utilities are probably overstated.** The pilot ran through winter, when heating and lighting cost most, so scaling it to a full year errs on the cautious side. This is "actual pilot spend," as the author says, but adjusted for season it would come out lower.

**The kiosk maintenance line is unexplained.** The extra hours are staffed, so it isn't clear why self-service kiosks need £7,500 of extra maintenance.

## 4. The self-service alternative is dismissed too quickly

- Self-service would save about two-thirds of staffing: roughly **£83,000 a year**.
- Building works cost **£300,000 once** (5 × £60,000). That pays back in about **3.6 years**, after which self-service is cheaper every year.
- "It would cost more" is true only over a short period, and it compares a one-off capital cost with an ongoing revenue cost, which usually come from different budgets.
- The bid also treats the choice as all or nothing. A mixed model is possible: staffed Sundays and staffed Thursday evenings for the job club, with self-service on Tuesday evenings.

## 5. What the pilot actually supports

Staff cost per visit, by time slot, at Ashgrove:

| Slot | Staff cost per hour | Visits per hour | Staff cost per visit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sunday 11–3 | £49.60 | 52 | **£0.95** |
| Tue/Thu 5–8 pm | £49.60 | 21 | **£2.36** |

At the busiest branch, Sunday hours cost about a third as much per visit as evening hours. At quieter branches, evening opening could easily cost £4 or more per visit, above the borough average the bid uses as its benchmark.

## Suggested changes before the bid goes to Members

1. Correct the total to £164,000, or show the missing £10,000 line.
2. Restate the evening finding accurately: about 40% of daytime use, with a fully booked job club.
3. Correct "twelve-month" to six months.
4. Show visit estimates for the other four branches based on their current use, not Ashgrove's.
5. Add leave cover to the staffing cost and explain the £24.80 rate.
6. Show the self-service comparison over five years, including a mixed option.
7. Consider phasing:
   - Sunday opening at all five branches.
   - Thursday evening opening with the job club at all five branches.
   - Tuesday evening opening only where branch data justify it.

    That would cost about half as much, keep the strongest pilot results, and allow evenings to be extended later if the six-month review supports it.
